top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct idea from the 2005 frequency comb and the 2012 control of single trapped ions: it cancels the trap light shift so many neutral atoms act as one clock. Independent laboratories agree near 1e-18, which establishes maturity, and the two-name credit (Katori for the proposal, Ye for the realization and accuracy) needs no arbitrary cut. The citation must name the magic-wavelength lattice, not timekeeping in general or the redefinition of the second. Overlap with earlier metrology prizes and the omission of Lemonde, Lisdat and Ludlow are real reservations but not disqualifying, so an award is preferable to no award.
